admission.justification: Three real ownership/error strategies were weighed; the conditional choice continues to constrain future refresh repairs and makes the deferred roster design explicit.

alternatives.option: A: tolerate and name an unrecognized file only when an own enclosure staged copy writes; otherwise fail and restore sources.
alternatives.reason: Keeps unrelated-file isolation and a named failure when no own copy ownership is established.

alternatives.option: B: fail every publication whenever an unreadable contract is encountered.
alternatives.reason: A broken unrelated file can again stop every task-document write.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A new owning ruling changes the requirement that unrelated files must not block an own publication.

alternatives.option: C: record an own-enclosure roster at creation so ownership survives corruption without reading the contract.
alternatives.reason: A cleaner ownership construction, explicitly outside this corrective leaf.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The owning hierarchy admits the roster design, or a damaged own enclosure remains stale without a named outcome.

consequences: No roster or new store is introduced.
At least one staged own enclosure does not establish the ownership of every unreadable neighbor.
Matching readable own-contract parse errors and copy-publication failures retain rollback.
context: An unparseable enclosure-position file cannot say whether it is own or unrelated; unconditional failure recreates the unrelated-file publication outage, while unconditional tolerance could silently abandon own copies.
decider: architect 97e0320d-431f-4f4c-8c86-66a6dca880a7 under D47; L134 ruling A
